runs.market_commentary: Asian markets closed mixed overnight. Japan's Nikkei surged 1.8% to 39,242, benefiting from a weaker yen and positive global risk appetite, while the Hang Seng dipped 1.6% as Chinese tech remained under pressure. The Reserve Bank of Australia held its cash rate at 4.35% in a hawkish hold, citing sticky services inflation, weighing on AUD-denominated assets. The region's session was underpinned by reports of nascent diplomatic progress on US-Iran Strait of Hormuz tensions, which briefly erased earlier oil gains. European markets opened cautiously. The DAX edged down 12 points to 26,311 while the FTSE 100 slipped to 10,858. German industrial data disappointed, reinforcing concerns about Eurozone growth divergence from the US. Energy stocks provided modest support amid elevated Brent crude, but defensives lagged as investors rotated toward risk assets on easing rate-hike fears. In the US pre-market, S&P 500 futures are up 0.2% and Nasdaq 100 futures are gaining 0.4% as July payrolls came in at -23,000, well below expectations, reducing the probability of another Fed rate hike. The dollar index firmed 0.21% to 99.748 as yields ticked higher ahead of tomorrow's pivotal CPI print (consensus: +0.1% MoM, +3.4% YoY). WTI crude hovers near $82.15 on Hormuz risk premium but has pared earlier gains on diplomatic optimism. Gold hit $4,402/oz (+1.40%), reflecting lingering safe-haven demand. The S&P 500 closed Monday at 7,753, pausing after a run of all-time highs. Market breadth was bifurcated — homebuilders (XHB +1.81%) and regional banks (KRE +1.11%) led, while megacap tech was mixed with Meta rising and Alphabet falling. Tomorrow's CPI is the single most important near-term catalyst, with a hot print risking a sharp reversal in rate-sensitive names.

ideas.catalyst: Argus upgraded Boeing to Buy with a $265 price target, citing superior long-term commercial aerospace prospects.
ideas.thesis: Boeing's narrowbody backlog extends well into the 2030s, providing multi-year earnings visibility as production ramps normalize. The upgrade follows stabilizing labor relations and improving 737 MAX delivery cadence, which should drive EPS multiple re-rating.
ideas.key_risk: Any new production halt or quality-control incident could trigger swift multiple compression.

ideas.catalyst: Gold rallied 1.40% to $4,402/oz as traders trimmed rate-cut bets ahead of Wednesday CPI and Strait of Hormuz tensions persisted.
ideas.thesis: A multi-factor tailwind — geopolitical risk premium, elevated inflation expectations, and central bank accumulation — provides a durable structural bid for gold. Tomorrow's CPI print creates an asymmetric opportunity: a miss keeps gold elevated while a beat merely causes a temporary dip to re-accumulate.
ideas.key_risk: A materially hot CPI print could spark a dollar surge and short-term gold correction of 2-3%.

ideas.catalyst: Goldman Sachs added Aon to its August Conviction List with a $430 price target, representing ~21% upside from current levels.
ideas.thesis: Aon is positioned to deliver above-consensus 2026 organic growth driven by the ongoing hard insurance market and expanding risk advisory demand. Free cash flow conversion is high, and the company's analytical platforms are increasingly sticky with large enterprise clients.
ideas.key_risk: A macro slowdown reducing corporate spending on discretionary risk management could pressure revenue growth.

ideas.catalyst: UBS upgraded Jabil to Buy with a $430 price target, highlighting AI infrastructure buildout as a key demand driver.
ideas.thesis: Jabil's contract manufacturing role in AI server and networking hardware gives it secular exposure to the capex cycle without the valuation premium of chip designers. Margin improvement in its intelligent infrastructure segment has been consistent across last three quarters.
ideas.key_risk: Customer concentration risk — loss of a major hyperscaler program could significantly impair earnings.

ideas.catalyst: XHB surged 1.81% today as July payrolls missed sharply at -23,000, sharply reducing rate-hike expectations.
ideas.thesis: Homebuilder stocks have significant operating leverage to any improvement in mortgage affordability; even a modest decline in the 10-year from 4.42% to 4.20% materially expands the buyer pool. A benign CPI tomorrow could extend today's rally with another 2-3% move.
ideas.key_risk: A hot CPI print reversing rate-cut expectations would erase today's gains quickly given the sector's rate sensitivity.

ideas.catalyst: Phillip Securities upgraded Spotify to Buy with a $650 price target, citing ARPU expansion from podcast and audiobook monetization.
ideas.thesis: Spotify's successive price increases have shown minimal churn, validating pricing power that most analysts had underestimated. The transition from music-only to audio-plus positions the platform to capture incremental ad dollars as podcast ad rates approach radio-equivalent CPMs.
ideas.key_risk: Intensified competition from Apple Music's spatial audio offerings or YouTube's ad-supported tier could slow premium subscriber growth.

ideas.catalyst: Riot reported strong Q2 financial results, sending shares sharply higher in pre-market trading.
ideas.thesis: Bitcoin mining economics remain favorable given current BTC price levels and Riot's low-cost energy contracts in Texas. A Q2 beat on hashrate expansion signals operational discipline that the market has historically rewarded with a 2-3 turn multiple premium vs. peers.
ideas.key_risk: Bitcoin price is the dominant variable — a 20%+ drawdown would overwhelm any operational improvements.

ideas.catalyst: WTI crude holding near $82 on Strait of Hormuz risk premium; energy sector leading small-caps today.
ideas.thesis: Occidental's Permian Basin concentration makes it a high-beta play on oil price, with the added optionality of Berkshire Hathaway's continued stake providing valuation floor. Hormuz tensions historically add $5-8 of geopolitical risk premium to WTI that can persist for weeks.
ideas.key_risk: A diplomatic resolution reopening the Strait could collapse the geopolitical premium and send WTI down 5-8% rapidly.

ideas.catalyst: Truist upgraded Best Buy to Buy with a $95 price target; homebuilder surge (XHB +1.81%) signals consumer confidence improvement.
ideas.thesis: Best Buy is a levered play on consumer spending normalization — as mortgage activity recovers on lower rates, appliance and home-electronics replacement cycles accelerate. The upgrade signals institutional confidence in margin stabilization after two years of cost cuts.
ideas.key_risk: A consumer spending slowdown or a hot CPI print dashing rate-cut hopes would hit the stock disproportionately.

ideas.catalyst: KLXE gapped down 32% after announcing a $125 million rights offering at a steep discount to reduce debt.
ideas.thesis: Dilutive equity raises at distressed prices signal balance sheet stress and management desperation — even in a supportive oil price environment, the overhang from new shares will suppress any sustained recovery. Rights offerings of this size relative to market cap typically require 6-8 weeks to fully digest.
ideas.key_risk: A sustained oil price spike and operational beat could cause a short squeeze given the high short interest that will build post-announcement.

deals.headline: Attovia Therapeutics Raises $289M in Upsized IPO; Shares Surge 29% on Debut
deals.description: US immunology biotech Attovia Therapeutics priced its IPO above the marketed range, raising $289 million in an upsized offering. The stock climbed approximately 29% on its first day of trading, reflecting strong institutional demand for clinical-stage immunology assets.

deals.headline: Londian Wason New Energy Tech IPO Priced on NYSE as FOIL at $20-22/Share
deals.description: Chinese manufacturer of electrolytic copper foil for lithium-ion batteries listed on the New York Stock Exchange under ticker FOIL, targeting gross proceeds of approximately $78.6 million at a $1.7 billion valuation. The listing represents increased capital market access for EV supply chain component manufacturers.

deals.headline: FDA Grants Accelerated Approval to Replimune's Tudriqev Oncolytic Immunotherapy
deals.description: The FDA granted accelerated approval to Tudriqev (vusolimogene oderparepvec-wtpg), an oncolytic immunotherapy developed by Replimune, closing out a regulatory saga that had twice ended in rejection. The approval opens a new treatment category for solid tumors and validates Replimune's platform after years of setbacks.

deals.headline: Takeda's Orzeyful (Oveporexton) Approved by FDA for Narcolepsy Type 1
deals.description: The US FDA approved Takeda's Orzeyful tablets for the treatment of narcolepsy type 1 in adults, representing the first orexin receptor agonist approved in this indication class. Takeda shares rose 3% to 5,425 yen on the Tokyo exchange following the announcement.

deals.headline: Adalvo and Gedeon Richter Expand Global Tirzepatide Partnership
deals.description: Malta-headquartered Adalvo and Hungary's Gedeon Richter announced an expanded global partnership to co-develop and supply therapies based on tirzepatide, the active ingredient of Eli Lilly's Mounjaro and Zepbound. The deal expands the competitive landscape for GLP-1/GIP dual-agonist therapies and signals confidence in biosimilar or follow-on pathways.
